title: Being Courteous
note: This is knowing the nature of everyone and getting along with them, without slipping yourself from greatness and worth. That is why it comes after those chapters.

couplets.plain: They say that being easy to approach, for anyone at all, makes the way of courtesy easy to reach.
couplets.pm: The books say that being easy for everyone to approach makes it easy to reach the rare good path called courtesy. For someone full of good qualities who is also approachable, courtesy comes of itself. It wins over the whole world, so the ancients made it a good path, and the books give this as the means.

links.quote: being easy to approach, for anyone at all

couplets.plain: Having loving-kindness and being born into a good family: these two are the way of courtesy.
couplets.pm: Having loving-kindness for others and being born in a family at one with the world: these two are the good path people call courtesy. Being born here means the conduct of those so born. Neither is enough alone, only both together.

links.quote: these two are the way of courtesy
links.reason: States what courtesy is made of: exactly two things together.
Loving-kindness is the first of the two.

links.quote: being born into a good family
links.reason: Birth in a good family is the second.

couplets.plain: Having the same limbs does not make people alike. True likeness is likeness in the courtesy that draws people close.
couplets.pm: Matching good people in body, which isn’t fit to hold close, isn’t true likeness. The likeness that fits is matching them in courtesy, which is. The body is separate from the soul and doesn’t last. Courtesy isn’t separate and does last. So have the courtesy they have.

links.quote: True likeness is likeness in the courtesy that draws people close
links.reason: Refuses the body as the measure of a person: courtesy is the only true likeness.

couplets.plain: The world praises the courtesy of those who are useful because they care for justice and for doing good.
couplets.pm: The world celebrates the courtesy of those who, loving justice and righteousness, are of use to others and themselves. Their justice, their goodness and their usefulness all come from courtesy, so that is what the world praises.

couplets.plain: Scorn hurts, even in fun. Those who know what others feel stay courteous, even in enmity.
couplets.pm: Being scorned hurts a person even in play. So those who live knowing others’ natures keep only pleasant ways, even where there is enmity. Knowing that hurt, they won’t cause it. He rejects readings that leave the two halves unconnected, or that take “hurts” to mean “doesn’t arise”.

links.reason: Those who know what others feel stay courteous even towards an enemy.

couplets.plain: The world goes on because of the courteous. Without them it would sink into the earth and die.
couplets.pm: The ways of the world go on for ever because they rest on the courteous. If they didn’t rest there, they would sink into the earth and perish. The discourteous give them no support, so only this has spared them from that end.

links.quote: The world goes on because of the courteous
links.reason: Credits the courteous with keeping the world going at all.

couplets.plain: Those without human courtesy are like trees, even if they are as sharp as a file.
couplets.pm: Those without the courtesy proper to good people are like a tree, which has only one sense, even if they are as sharp as a file. A file wears down what it touches and isn’t worn itself. A tree lacks higher knowledge, and since they lack the courtesy that knowledge should yield, they lack it too.

links.reason: Sharp wits count for nothing once human courtesy is missing.
Gives clever people the keen edge of a file, an edge with nothing human behind it.
Makes those without courtesy trees: dull timber set against the file’s bite.

couplets.plain: Even towards those who won’t be friends and treat you unkindly, it is low to fail in courtesy.
couplets.pm: Even towards those who refuse friendship and act as enemies, it is a blot on the wise not to keep to courtesy. Do that and you become like them, which is why he says “low”.
couplets.sensitive: asks courtesy towards those who mistreat you

links.quote: it is low to fail in courtesy
links.reason: Holds that discourtesy lowers you even when the other person has been unkind.

couplets.plain: To those who can’t laugh, the vast wide world lies in darkness, even by day.
couplets.pm: For those who, lacking courtesy, can’t mix with anyone and feel glad inside, the whole great world lies in darkness even in daytime. Because they never mix with people, they can’t know the ways of the world. Some read the ending differently, as “the darkness hasn’t left”.
couplets.sensitive: can read as condemning the depressed

links.quote: lies in darkness, even by day
links.reason: To those who can’t laugh the whole world lies in darkness, though it is day.

couplets.plain: The great wealth gained by someone without courtesy is like good milk gone sour from a bad pot.
couplets.pm: Great wealth that someone without courtesy has gained through past good deeds goes to waste, of no use to anyone because of that fault, as good cow’s milk spoils through a fault in its vessel. “Gained” shows he can’t create wealth himself. This points ahead to the next chapter.

links.quote: like good milk gone sour from a bad pot
links.reason: Someone without courtesy spoils great wealth the way a bad pot spoils good milk.

ideaLinks.reason: Loving-kindness is one of the two things that make up courtesy.

ideaLinks.quote: being born into a good family
ideaLinks.reason: Birth in a good family must join loving-kindness before courtesy can appear.
